now.name: louis-agent
now.description: This year I've been learning AI engineering the hands-on way: every skill built, measured before and after, and written up. It runs this site, its guide in the corner and the Puls specialists on mypuls.co.za.
highlights: The engine: a streaming tool loop on Microsoft.Extensions.AI over Anthropic, OpenAI and Ollama, tools grouped in packs, usable from Rider (ACP), a Blazor app, an HTTP API, a CLI or as an MCP server. An orchestrator watches a service's errors, hands fixes to the coding agent, and checks each one itself: the commit, the failing request replayed, the tests run.
Evals in C#: one harness for every check, code graders first, an LLM judge only after it agreed with my own labels (35 of 36), replays that re-score for $0, and an eval studio to run them.
Every request measured: a usage ledger priced by a dated price table, shown in rand; prompt caching took a benchmark run from $0.66 to $0.13. OpenTelemetry traces per turn and tool call.
In production: an MCP server and ACP for Rider, arguments never through a shell, robots.txt obeyed in code, Azure Container Apps from Bicep, deployed by GitHub Actions after green CI.
